source.section: Instructions PDF pp.9-10, Schedule M line 1t, questions 1 and 2 and table lines 1-4; Instructions PDF p.4, RI-1040 lines 1-5; PDF p.5, lines 6-8; PDF p.13, Tax Computation Worksheet ('Use for all filing status types')

worked: Federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 60,000.00 + interest 47,000.01 = 107,000.01. Federal taxable income = 107,000.01 - 15,750.00 standard deduction - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65+ = 89,250.01 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). RI-1040 line 1 federal AGI 107,000.01. Line 1t: question 1 born on or before March 1, 1959: person 0 born 1955-06-15 (age 70): yes; question 2 federal AGI 107,000.01 less than or equal to 107,000.00: no. Not both yes: no table, modification 0.00. Line 1y total decreasing modifications = 0.00. Line 2a other-state obligations 0.00; line 2m total increasing modifications = 0.00. Schedule M page 2 line 3 net = 0.00 - 0.00 = 0.00; RI-1040 line 2 = 0.00. Line 3 modified federal AGI = 107,000.01 + (0.00) = 107,000.01. Standard Deduction and Exemption Worksheets: line 3 107,000.01 is not more than 254,250.00: the worksheets stop at line 3, full amounts. Line 4 standard deduction: 10,900.00 (Single). Line 5 = 107,000.01 - 10,900.00 = 96,100.01. Line 6 exemptions: 1 x 5,100.00 = 5,100.00. Line 7 taxable income = 96,100.01 - 5,100.00 = 91,000.01. Line 8 tax on 91,000.01 by the schedule as numbers: 79,900.00 x 0.0375 = 2996.2500 + 11,100.01 x 0.0475 = 527.250475 = 3523.500475, 3,523.50 to the cent. Credits 0.00 (Schedule I, Schedule II, RI earned income credit and RI-1040H are not modelled and not claimed here). Rhode Island income tax = 3,523.50. Note: One cent over the limit: the test is a cliff, so the whole 50,000 is lost.
